dimensions.assessment: Affects all federal agencies, state and local governments relying on grants from specific departments, and any individuals whose vehicle data might otherwise be collected or accessed by federal entities.
dimensions.evidence: the head of any Federal agency and any Federal official, in an official capacity, and any person acting on behalf of the Federal Government may not acquire, possess, access, or use in the United States

dimensions.assessment: Changes operational practices for federal law enforcement and data collection, introduces civil penalties and causes of action against the federal government, and withholds federal financial assistance from non-compliant state and local governments.
dimensions.evidence: a violation of this section shall constitute an injury to any individual aggrieved by a violation of this Act.

dimensions.assessment: Involves withholding federal grant funds from non-compliant state and local governments and requiring the repayment of federal funds used in violation of purchase prohibitions.
dimensions.evidence: Federal funds used in violation of this section shall be treated as an unallowable cost and shall be repaid to the United States.

dimensions.assessment: Imposes sweeping new statutory prohibitions across federal, state, and local entities regarding the acquisition, access, and use of automatic license plate readers and associated data.
dimensions.evidence: no Federal financial assistance administered... may be obligated, awarded, disbursed, or otherwise provided directly or indirectly, to a State or unit of local government unless...

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory restrictions taking effect on the first day of the first fiscal year following enactment and applying nationwide across all United States territories and possessions.
dimensions.evidence: Beginning on the first day of the first fiscal year beginning after the date of the enactment of this Act

importance_detail.rationale: The Ban Flock Act places nationwide restrictions on the use of automatic license plate readers and captured plate data by the Federal Government, with narrow exceptions for tolling and explicitly authorized activities. It also conditions major federal grants to State and local governments on enacting matching prohibitions and bans federal funds from purchasing or operating such readers.

summary: H.R. 10691, titled the "Ban Flock Act," prohibits the Federal Government from acquiring, possessing, accessing, or using automatic license plate readers (ALPRs) or data derived from them, unless explicitly authorized by an Act of Congress. It also withholds certain federal grants from State and local governments unless they ban ALPR use to the same or greater extent. Additionally, the bill prohibits the use of federal funds to purchase, lease, maintain, or upgrade ALPRs or to obtain captured plate data. Specific exceptions are made for tolling operations under strict limitations.

affected_groups.effect: Must stop acquiring, possessing, accessing, or using automatic license plate readers and captured plate data unless explicitly authorized by Congress or covered by the tolling exception.
Risk losing federal financial assistance from specific federal departments unless they enact laws or binding policies prohibiting ALPR use.
Permitted to use ALPRs solely for tolling purposes, but face strict requirements regarding data retention limits, security, and prohibitions on sharing data with law enforcement without a warrant.
Granted the right to sue the Federal Government for violations, seek damages or injunctive relief, and have unlawfully obtained data barred from use against them as evidence.

key_provisions: Prohibits the Federal Government from acquiring, possessing, accessing, or using automatic license plate readers or captured plate data without explicit statutory authorization.

Withholds federal financial assistance from the Departments of Justice, Transportation, Health and Human Services, Housing and Urban Development, and Homeland Security from any State or local government that does not ban ALPR use to the same or greater extent.
Bans the use of federal funds to purchase, lease, install, operate, maintain, upgrade, or contract for ALPRs and captured plate data.
Excludes ALPRs and data used solely for assessing, billing, collecting, auditing, disputing, or enforcing toll payments, subject to strict limitations on data use, sharing, and retention.

Provides a private right of action allowing individuals aggrieved by a violation to sue the Federal Government, and permits State attorneys general to bring civil actions on behalf of state residents.
Makes evidence obtained in violation of the federal ban inadmissible in federal investigations and proceedings.

It also withholds certain federal grants from State and local governments unless they ban ALPR use to the same or greater extent. summary_detail.significance: The bill represents a sweeping restriction on the use of surveillance technology by the federal government and creates a financial incentive for state and local governments to follow suit by conditioning federal grants on local bans of automatic license plate readers.
